title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Tender beef strips in a creamy mushroom and soured cream sauce
excerpt: Thin strips of beef fillet cooked quickly over high heat with mushrooms, onion, and a paprika-enriched soured cream sauce. A Russian classic that became globally popular after World War II.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef stroganoff is named after the Stroganov family, a powerful Russian noble dynasty. The dish appears in Russian cookbooks from the nineteenth century, using tender beef strips, mustard, and soured cream. Its international spread followed Russian émigrés and then spread further during the twentieth century through hotel and restaurant menus. Most Western versions include mushrooms, which were not in the original.

recipeTools.notes: Wide pan, the beef needs room to sear, not steam.

content.text: Beef stroganoff depends on cooking the beef very fast over very high heat so it sears rather than steams. If you crowd the pan the temperature drops and the beef stews. Cook in batches if necessary and set the beef aside while you make the sauce. Add it back only at the end, just to warm through. Fillet is traditional; sirloin is also excellent and more affordable.

items.preparation: cut into strips 1 cm x 5 cm

content.text: Season the beef generously. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large frying pan over very high heat. Cook the beef in a single layer without stirring for 1 minute, then toss and cook for 1 more minute. The beef should be browned but still pink inside. Remove immediately and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the butter and remaining oil. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until they release their liquid and it evaporates. Add the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute.

Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard. Stir and simmer for 3 minutes. Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the soured cream and season with salt and pepper. Do not let it boil or the cream will split.
Return the beef to the pan and warm through for 1 minute. Scatter with parsley and serve with egg noodles or rice.
